messages:
emma (AE): FinBankCo says they'll do a POC but legal flagged data residency as a hard blocker. They want: EU-only for normal ops, DR-only failover allowed with audit, BYO-KMS (Azure Key Vault), and the EU subprocessor roster. Need answers + pricing impact by EOW so deal doesn't slip.

kai (Solutions Eng): Quick clarifying Qs — is the 'DR-only' fallback acceptable if we require manual activation and documented incident steps? Also which BYO-KMS pattern: customer-managed cloud KMS or on-prem HSM?

emma (AE): They're fine with DR-only as long as it's documented in the contract: "normal operations remain EU-only; DR allowed under documented incident response and audit." BYO-KMS = Azure KV.

anika (Security PM): We can provide an EU subprocessor list and our SOC2/ISO attestation. For BYO-KMS we'll need the customer to provision the key and grant a Redwood service principal the minimal wrapping/unwrap permissions. We'll also need to include a short MOU for key lifecycle/rotation and emergency access — I can draft it.

ryan (Runtime Eng): From a runtime standpoint we have two practical modes: tenant pinning to an EU Dedicated pool (strongest guarantee) or region-affinity routing with an explicit DR fallback tier. Tenant pinning is easier to reason about for legal but usually requires reserved capacity. Geofence/affinity gives autoscaling benefits but is a softer guarantee. Pricing/ops tradeoffs apply.

luis (Sales Eng): Can you show the customer a tiny sample routing policy to make the 'EU primary + DR manual' behavior explicit?

ryan (Runtime Eng): Yep, sample policy we can include in the tech appendix:
```
{"policy":"region_affinity","rules":[{"match":"tenant==FinBankCo","primary":"eu-west-1","fallback":"apac-sg-1","fallback_mode":"manual","note":"fallback only for DR with written approval"}]}
```
This enforces EU primary routing and requires a manual activation step for fallback.

anika (Security PM): We'll attach the subproc attestation and a BYO-KMS checklist. I'll upload both and start the MOU draft. cc @legal-bot

legal-bot: Uploaded EU-subproc-attestation_v1.pdf and BYO-KMS_MOU_draft.docx to /shared/finbankco/docs (permissions: sales+sec+legal).

emma (AE): Great. Customer also needs a ballpark on pricing delta for 'standby failover' vs 'dedicated EU pinned' so they can decide which commit to sign.

ryan (Runtime Eng): Ballpark notes: hosted EU with DR-on-demand = base usage + DR egress / cross-region burst overhead -> roughly base + 15–25% depending on expected DR frequency. Dedicated EU (tenant pin/reserved capacity) = base + reserved capacity premium ~ +35–50% depending on SLA and capacity headroom. Exact numbers need their QPS/traffic profile.

luis (Sales Eng): I'll ask FinBankCo for peak QPS, retention and acceptable RTO for DR. Recommended POC timeline to present: 2w setup (subproc docs + KMS provisioning + routing policy), 1w validation (routing dry-run + audit logs) — total ~3w.

emma (AE): Please escalate to eng-oncall for a capacity sanity check and confirm if any special infra is needed for Azure KV integration. EOW delivery, please.

ryan (Runtime Eng): Escalating to eng-oncall now. tagging @ops-oncall to confirm EU pool headroom and whether we need dedicated nodes for tenant pin. I'll report back once they confirm.

kai (Solutions Eng): I'll own the POC runbook and schedule kickoff for next Tue. Will coordinate test cases (normal ops, DR activation, audit trail verification). :thumbsup:

luis (Sales Eng): Keeping customer in the loop. Will send an interim note: "we can support EU-first with documented DR fallback; we will share subproc attestations and a BYO-KMS MOU; final pricing depends on QPS — please send traffic profile."

emma (AE): Thanks team — priority: keep this from slipping. Ping me on any blocker.
